label: History
value: Anne was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia to high school teacher Walter Shirley and Bertha Shirley, Anne was orphaned as an infant. She spent a harsh childhood living with Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and at an orphan asylum before being brought to Green Gables by Matthew Cuthbert and Marilla Cuthbert. In Avonlea, she formed a lifelong friendship with Diana Barry and maintained an intense academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe. After attending Queen's Academy and earning her teacher's license, she won the Avery Scholarship and later taught school in Avonlea, during which time she helped found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Anne proceeded to Redmond College, where she earned her B.A. degree and won the Thorburn Scholarship in English. Following three years of teaching school in Summerside, she married Gilbert Blythe and settled in Four Winds, eventually giving birth to a son, Little Jem.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye was taken in as an orphan nephew.
unit: Anthony Pye was taken in as an orphan nephew by his aunt, Mrs. George Pye, and began attending school under Anne Shirley. On his early days at school, he poured water down Aurelia Clay's neck from his slate bottle, for which Anne kept him in at recess to lecture him on being a gentleman, though he remained completely untouched. Unlike the other pupils, Anthony openly disliked Anne and held her in contempt because she was a female teacher. He continued to show mockery and disrespect in class, such as strutting impertinently and grinning at her. On one occasion, he watched mockingly as Anne opened her desk drawer to find a mouse that had been placed inside. Anne subsequently punished him with a pointer until tears came to his eyes.

value: Aunt Jamesina is sweet
unit: Aunt Jamesina is sweet, cheerful, and holds quaint, old-fashioned views while remaining indulgent and easygoing. She possesses mirthful, twinkling young eyes and a philosophy of doing her duty while having a good time. She is deeply affectionate toward the girls she housemothers, even when she finds their behavior baffling. Though respectful of the clergy, she harbors a playful side, admitting she used to make fun of her suitors.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews drove Anne Shirley, Diana, and Jane to the White Sands concert.
unit: Billy Andrews drove Anne Shirley, Diana, and his sister Jane to the White Sands concert in his double-seated buggy, insisting that Anne ride on the front seat beside him. During the evening's supper, Billy decamped in mortal fear of receiving an invitation, though he waited outside with the team to drive the girls home. Having always admired Anne, he later sought to marry her once his father gave him the upper farm in his own name. Too shy to propose himself, he badgered his sister Jane into proposing to Anne on his behalf, offering to wait until she finished college. Following Anne's refusal, Billy did not break his heart and instead married Nettie Blewett, beaming with pride and happiness when he introduced his new bride to the parish church congregation.

unit: Billy Andrews drove Anne Shirley, Diana, and his sister Jane to the White Sands concert in his double-seated buggy, insisting that Anne ride on the front seat beside him. During the evening's supper, Billy decamped in mortal fear of receiving an invitation, though he waited outside with the team to drive the girls home. Having always admired Anne, he later sought to marry her once his father gave him the upper farm in his own name. Too shy to propose himself, he badgered his sister Jane into proposing to Anne on his behalf, offering to wait until she finished college. Following Anne's refusal, Billy did not break his heart and instead married Nettie Blewett, beaming with pride and happiness when he introduced his new bride to the parish church congregation.

value: > ‘Captain Jim’ is my week-a-day name and you might as well begin as you’re sartain to end up—calling me that.

label: Quotes
value: > You’re young and I’m old, but our souls are about the same age, I reckon. We both belong to the race that knows Joseph, as Cornelia Bryant would say.

value: > I saved his life, and when you’ve saved a creature’s life you’re bound to love it. It’s next thing to giving life.

value: Captain Jim is a high-souled man.
unit: He is a high-souled, simple-minded, and cheerful man who possesses an unshakeable placidity and hospitality. A passionate worshipper of beauty, every lovely sight or sound brings him subtle inner joy, though he lamentably lacks outward comeliness himself. He possesses a quaint wisdom, eternal youth in his heart, and a chronic habit of enjoying life.

label: History
value: At sixteen, Captain Jim formed a close friendship with John Selwyn.
unit: At sixteen, Captain Jim formed a close friendship with John Selwyn, the Glen schoolmaster who taught him a lifelong love of poetry. Driven by a sea-going heritage, he ran off to sea and spent most of his life sailing the world before retiring five years prior to keep the lighthouse at Four Winds Point. During his sea-faring years, he lost his beloved sweetheart Margaret when her dory drifted out to sea during a storm. In a Havana boarding house, he discovered an amnesiac Dick Moore and returned him to his wife Leslie. In his elder years, he kept the Four Winds light alongside his nephew Alec and welcomed Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe to the shore, quickly becoming a beloved friend and companion. He shared his life-book of experiences with visiting author Owen Ford, who collaborated with him to turn it into a published book. After seeing the book accepted and watching Anne and Gilbert name their son after him, Captain Jim peacefully passed away.

label: History
value: Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge.
unit: Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge as a fourteen-year-old handmaiden to Miss Lavendar Lewis, taking her board and clothes as the fourth sister in her family to serve the household. She developed a deep affection for Miss Lavendar and welcomed guests like Anne Shirley and Diana Barry with great cheerfulness. When Miss Lavendar prepared to marry Stephen Irving, Charlotta assisted enthusiastically with the wedding preparations before moving with the newlyweds to Boston. Though initially homesick in Boston and preferring Prince Edward Island, she returned with the Irvings to Echo Lodge during subsequent summers. She later married a good-tempered bricklayer named Tom, and eventually attended Anne Shirley's wedding, where she happily threw rice and old shoes for the bride and groom.

Following her brother's early death in his twenties and the rejection of various suitors in her youth, she settled into life as an outspoken old maid in Four Winds. She developed strong friendships with her neighbor Leslie Moore, Captain Jim, and Doctor Dave. Upon the arrival of Gilbert and Anne Blythe, Cornelia immediately struck up a warm friendship with Anne and spent much of her time visiting their home, sewing elaborate clothes for neglected neighborhood babies, and entertaining them with sharp commentary. During Anne's illness and recovery, Cornelia spent a great deal of her time cooking delicacies for her. Later, to the surprise of neighbors who knew her anti-male rhetoric, she accepted a marriage proposal from her long-time acquaintance Marshall Elliott.

value: Davy and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy and his twin sister Dora were orphaned after their mother died, having lost their father as an infant. Marilla Cuthbert took them into Green Gables, where Davy quickly earned a reputation for mischief and endless questions. Anne Shirley took a maternal interest in him, successfully using patience and affection to encourage him to be good. Davy began attending Avonlea school alongside his desk mate Milty Boulter and competed over height with him. As he grew older, he was considered a smart boy who settled into better habits, though he retained a love for violent stories and a strong political interest as a Conservative.

label: History
value: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope
unit: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope with her parents and younger sister Minnie May. As a child, she swore an oath of eternal friendship with Anne Shirley. After unintentionally becoming intoxicated on currant wine at Green Gables, her mother briefly forbade her from playing with Anne, but Mrs. Barry relented after Anne cured Minnie May's croup. Diana attended Avonlea school, joined a Story Club with her schoolmates, and took part in local concerts and outings. Unlike Anne, she did not attend Queen's Academy or Redmond College, remaining in Avonlea where she served as treasurer for the Village Improvement Society. In her late teens, she became engaged to Fred Wright and eventually married him at Orchard Slope. Together they established a home and had two children, little Fred and Small Anne Cordelia.

label: History
value: Dick worked in Abner's store during the winters.
unit: Dick worked in his father Abner's store during the winters and sailed during the summers. He became infatuated with Leslie West due to her beauty and her refusal to speak to him, eventually coercing her mother into pressuring Leslie into marriage. After living with Leslie for one winter on the West place, Dick grew tired of settled life and went to Nova Scotia to visit relatives. He subsequently embarked on a voyage to Havana on the vessel Four Sisters alongside his cousin, George Moore. Thirteen years prior to Captain Jim's discovery of his cousin in Cuba, Dick died of yellow fever in Cuba.

label: History
value: Dora's father died.
unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy were orphaned at a young age after their father died and their sick mother passed away. Marilla Cuthbert took them into Green Gables, where Dora proved to be an exceptionally well-behaved, obedient, and helpful child compared to her mischievous brother. She began attending school alongside Davy and made friends, such as planning to sit with Lily Sloane. Over the years, she grew into a sensible, careful, and womanly fifteen-year-old girl who assisted around Green Gables. When Anne Shirley left Green Gables after her marriage, Dora was chosen to inherit Anne's former porch room.

unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy were orphaned at a young age after their father died and their sick mother passed away. Marilla Cuthbert took them into Green Gables, where Dora proved to be an exceptionally well-behaved, obedient, and helpful child compared to her mischievous brother. She began attending school alongside Davy and made friends, such as planning to sit with Lily Sloane. Over the years, she grew into a sensible, careful, and womanly fifteen-year-old girl who assisted around Green Gables. When Anne Shirley left Green Gables after her marriage, Dora was chosen to inherit Anne's former porch room.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe grows up in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island.
unit: Gilbert Blythe grows up in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, returning to school after spending three years in Alberta with his ailing father. Upon returning, he becomes the academic rival of Anne Shirley after teasing her by calling her 'Carrots.' Though Anne holds a grudge against him for years, Gilbert repeatedly attempts to apologize and secretly holds deep affection for her, even saving her from a sinking dory. He earns his First Class teacher's license at Queen's Academy and generously surrenders his teaching post at Avonlea to Anne, taking a job at White Sands instead. During his teaching years, he co-founds the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and decides to pursue a career in medicine. Gilbert attends Redmond College alongside Anne, where he excels academically, is elected Freshman Class President, and captains the football team. He proposes to Anne in their second year at Redmond, but she initially rejects him, leading to a distant period where Gilbert focuses on his studies, works for the Daily News, and is rumored to be courting Christine Stuart. After graduating with High Honors and the Cooper Prize, he falls dangerously ill with typhoid fever; upon learning that Anne loves him, he recovers rapidly and they become engaged. Gilbert completes his medical degree and takes over the practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Blythe, in Four Winds Harbor. He marries Anne at Green Gables and settles into a small house o' dreams, establishing a highly successful medical practice by saving patients like Rhoda Allonby and earning the deep respect of the community.

label: History
value: Mr. Harrison moved from New Brunswick to Avonlea
unit: After moving from New Brunswick to Avonlea in early April, Mr. Harrison lived as a bachelor on his farm, hiring young John Henry Carter to assist him. He quickly gained a reputation as an eccentric crank due to his irregular meals and his foul-mouthed parrot, Ginger. Shortly after his arrival, he angrily confronted Anne Shirley over a Jersey cow that had escaped into his grain, though the two quickly patched things up and became good friends. While keeping his past separation from his wife Emily a secret, he was rumored by local gossips to be courting Isabella Andrews when he merely visited her home to play checkers with Harmon Andrews. Eventually, his wife Emily relocated to Avonlea to reunite with him following the death of Ginger, after which Mr. Harrison transformed his habits, attending church regularly and dressing neatly. He maintained a close friendship with Anne, offering honest, blunt feedback on her early writing efforts before she left for college.

value: Jane is composed.
unit: Jane is a composed, practical, sensible, and unflappable person who remains unbothered by nerves during examinations. She lacks imaginative or poetical tendencies, viewing poems strictly as lines and verses, and is known for never saying anything that would hurt anyone's feelings.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea as part of the local youth cohort, participating in school activities and forming the Story Club with Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Ruby Gillis. While studying under Miss Stacy for the Queen's Entrance examination, she prepared for a teaching career and excelled in domestic science at Queen's Academy. Upon earning her teaching license, she was hired by the Newbridge school, where her disciplined methods earned her a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. She joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, serving on fundraising and morale committees with her peers. After later taking over the Avonlea school and eventually resigning, she traveled west to teach on the prairies. During a winter visit home, she reluctantly conveyed a marriage proposal to Anne on behalf of her shy brother Billy. She later returned to Avonlea and married Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, departing on a wedding tour to Europe before settling into a prosperous life in Winnipeg.

label: History
value: Josie attended Avonlea school
unit: Josie attended Avonlea school under Mr. Phillips and Miss Stacy, where she was the last of the Pye family to attend. During a school spelling match, she cheated by looking at her book, drawing Anne Shirley's scorn. She excelled at walking board fences and successfully walked the Barry fence on a dare, which she had issued after daring Jane Andrews to hop on one leg. When preparing for a local concert, Josie grew sulky because she was denied the role of fairy queen due to her figure, and she insulted Anne's hair in retaliation. Later, she ceased speaking to Julia Bell for three months after making a rude comment about Julia's recitation bow. At the Exhibition, Josie won first prize for her knitted lace. She prepared for the Queen's College entrance examinations—telling classmates she wished to attend college purely for education's sake—and went on to achieve preeminence at Queen's Academy as the sharpest-tongued student. When Anne returned to college after winning a prize story contest, Josie out of envy accused Anne of copying the story from an old paper.

label: Appearance
value: Lavendar Lewis is a petite lady.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis grew up in East Grafton.
unit: Lavendar Lewis grew up in East Grafton, where her father named her after the lavender scent he associated with her mother. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but the engagement ended after a foolish quarrel fueled by mutual pride and her own sulkiness. After Stephen left for the United States, she spent decades living a quiet, romantic life at Echo Lodge, taking in a succession of young Bowman handmaidens whom she collectively nicknamed Charlotta. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited Echo Lodge, Miss Lavendar formed a deep friendship with Anne, recognizing her as a kindred spirit. Through Anne's introduction, she met Stephen's son, Paul Irving, which inadvertently led to Stephen learning she remained unmarried and returning to seek her forgiveness. The two reconciled and were married in a ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor before moving to Boston. She later returned to Prince Edward Island for visits, maintaining a loving stepmother relationship with Paul and an enduring closeness with Anne.

After Stephen left for the United States, she spent decades living a quiet, romantic life at Echo Lodge, taking in a succession of young Bowman handmaidens whom she collectively nicknamed Charlotta. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited Echo Lodge, Miss Lavendar formed a deep friendship with Anne, recognizing her as a kindred spirit. Through Anne's introduction, she met Stephen's son, Paul Irving, which inadvertently led to Stephen learning she remained unmarried and returning to seek her forgiveness. The two reconciled and were married in a ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor before moving to Boston. She later returned to Prince Edward Island for visits, maintaining a loving stepmother relationship with Paul and an enduring closeness with Anne.

label: History
value: Leslie grew up in Four Winds.
unit: Leslie grew up in Four Winds, enduring early family tragedies when her younger brother died in an accident and her father committed suicide. After attending Queen's Academy and teaching school, she was coerced at sixteen into marrying Dick Moore to keep her mother from being evicted from her home. Following her mother's death and Dick's departure at sea, Dick returned as a brain-damaged invalid, whom Leslie loyally cared for over eleven years in quiet poverty. Upon becoming close friends with Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe, she agreed to Gilbert's suggestion to take Dick to Montreal for brain surgery. The operation revealed that the man was actually Dick's double-cousin, George Moore, leaving Leslie free from her tragic marriage. She fell in love with Owen Ford, who later proposed to her, and she subsequently planned her future alongside her beloved friends.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived her entire life at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived her entire life at Green Gables with her brother Matthew. In middle age, they decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, but a mistake resulted in the arrival of Anne Shirley. Though initially intent on rectifying the mistake, Marilla decided to keep Anne, resolving to raise her with proper discipline and moral training. Over the years, Marilla grew deeply attached to the imaginative girl, supporting her education up through Queen's Academy and college. Following Matthew's sudden death, Marilla faced the loss of Green Gables' main caretaker and began suffering from failing eyes and severe headaches. In later years, she took in her orphaned distant relatives, the Keith twins Davy and Dora, raising them alongside Rachel Lynde after Mrs. Lynde moved into Green Gables. Marilla saw Anne graduate, embark on her teaching career, and eventually marry Gilbert Blythe. In her later years, she traveled for the first time away from home to visit Anne at Four Winds for Christmas and returned in the spring to help attend to her after childbirth.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was born a Grit.
unit: Born a Grit, Marshall Elliott campaigned intensely for his political party during a particularly bitter general election fifteen years earlier. Confident in a Liberal victory, he made a public vow not to shave his face or cut his hair until the Grits achieved power. Following their defeat, he steadfastly kept his word for fifteen years despite his eccentric appearance. Over the years, he maintained a friendship with Captain Jim, occasionally joining him for cod-fishing and visiting the Four Winds Lighthouse. During one New Year's Eve celebration at the lighthouse, he entertained the company by singing old Scotch ballads and dancing gracefully with Leslie Moore. When the Liberals finally won a general election, he quietly left the store where the election news arrived and woke up the local barber in the middle of the night to shave his beard and cut his hair. Afterwards, he became betrothed to Miss Cornelia Bryant.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet life.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet, retired life at Green Gables with his sister Marilla. Deciding to adopt a young orphan boy to help him with farm chores in his older years, Matthew drove to Bright River station, only to find Anne Shirley waiting instead. Despite his dread of little girls, Matthew was quickly won over by Anne's lively chatter and silently insisted on keeping her. Over the years, he formed a deep bond with Anne as her quiet champion, buying her a pretty dress for a school concert and giving her a little calf of her own. As his heart trouble worsened, he continued to work despite warnings. Upon receiving news of the failure of the Abbey Bank, Matthew suffered a fatal heart attack and died instantly on the doorstep of Green Gables. He was buried in the Avonlea graveyard, where Anne regularly visited his grave.

Deciding to adopt a young orphan boy to help him with farm chores in his older years, Matthew drove to Bright River station, only to find Anne Shirley waiting instead. Despite his dread of little girls, Matthew was quickly won over by Anne's lively chatter and silently insisted on keeping her. Over the years, he formed a deep bond with Anne as her quiet champion, buying her a pretty dress for a school concert and giving her a little calf of her own. As his heart trouble worsened, he continued to work despite warnings. Upon receiving news of the failure of the Abbey Bank, Matthew suffered a fatal heart attack and died instantly on the doorstep of Green Gables. He was buried in the Avonlea graveyard, where Anne regularly visited his grave.

value: Owen Ford had a severe bout of typhoid fever in the spring.
unit: Following a severe bout of typhoid fever in the spring, Owen Ford was advised by his doctor to recuperate by the sea. He traveled to Four Winds to visit the original home of his maternal grandparents. While there, he befriended Anne Blythe, Gilbert Blythe, and Captain Jim Boyd. After hearing Captain Jim's life experiences, Owen agreed to collaborate with him on writing a biographical book. During his stay, he fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore. Recognizing her difficult marriage, he initially confessed his feelings to Anne and left Four Winds to avoid causing trouble. He completed the life-book, titled 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim', which was accepted for publication. He later returned from Vancouver to Four Winds to court Leslie after her circumstances changed.

label: History
value: Phil met Anne Shirley during her freshman year at Redmond College.
unit: Phil met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant during her freshman year at Redmond College, quickly drawing them into her vast social circle and helping them acclimate to Kingsport. For a long time, she was indecisive between two suitors from home, Alec and Alonzo, treating them both as playful chums. During her sophomore year, she moved into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina, learning basic domestic skills such as sweeping and marketing. She eventually met Jonas Blake, a minister and fellow Redmond graduate, falling deeply in love with him and committing to study mathematics to prove her cleverness to him. Despite initial opposition from her mother, Phil remained firm, gained her family's approval, and married Jonas the week after her graduation, with Anne serving as her bridesmaid. Later, she wrote a letter to Gilbert Blythe letting him know Anne was not engaged to Roy Gardner, encouraging him to try again. Prior to Anne's wedding, she visited Green Gables with her husband, and she later innocently sent Anne a congratulatory letter about her newborn, unaware that the infant had tragically died.

value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea. During his tenure, he boarded at Eben Wright's house near the school. In class, he frequently used whipping as a punishment for infractions, such as when Sam Boulter spoke back to him, leading Sam's father to confront him directly. On Anne Shirley's first day of school, he humiliated her publicly by holding up her slate due to poor spelling, and later punished her for her temper by forcing her to stand on the platform in front of the blackboard. Mr. Phillips spent much of his instructional effort hearing Latin and preparing older students like Prissy Andrews for Queen's, while neglecting the younger children and allowing general classroom order to slide. During a Mayflower gathering with the scholars, he gathered flowers to give to Prissy Andrews while addressing her with quotes from books.

On Anne Shirley's first day of school, he humiliated her publicly by holding up her slate due to poor spelling, and later punished her for her temper by forcing her to stand on the platform in front of the blackboard. Mr. Phillips spent much of his instructional effort hearing Latin and preparing older students like Prissy Andrews for Queen's, while neglecting the younger children and allowing general classroom order to slide. During a Mayflower gathering with the scholars, he gathered flowers to give to Prissy Andrews while addressing her with quotes from books.

label: History
value: Priscilla attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla attended Queen's Academy, where she became part of a close-knit circle of intimate friends with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. After graduating, she taught school in her home district. During her time on Prince Edward Island, she joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, preparing and reading a paper on cemeteries for one of their meetings. Later, she persuaded her father to let her attend Redmond College in Kingsport, arriving early to board with Anne Shirley. Along with Anne, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, she lived at Patty's Place while studying classics during her college years. Following her time at Redmond, Priscilla married a handsome, well-dressed foreign missionary who admired her beauty, and relocated with him to Japan.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel manages her own affairs
unit: Mrs. Rachel is a highly capable, practical, and energetic woman who manages her own affairs and freely manages those of her neighbors. Extremely outspoken, blunt, and opinionated, she prides herself on always speaking her mind without fear or favor. Though often regarded as a gossipy, severe, and bossy busybody, she possesses a good, kind heart and acts as a devoted, uncomplaining nurse when needed. She is a dedicated church member and a passionate politician who holds strong prejudices and believes in foreordination.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for forty-five years in Lynde's Hollow near Green Gables.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for forty-five years in Lynde's Hollow near Green Gables, managing her home, raising her family, and taking an active role in church societies and local politics. When Marilla Cuthbert adopted Anne Shirley, Rachel initially criticized Anne's looks and temper, leading to a clash before the two reconciled. Over the years, she offered advice to Matthew and Marilla, helped sew dresses for Anne, and took home first prize for butter and cheese at the Exhibition. After her husband Thomas grew ill and died, Rachel learned that their farm was heavily mortgaged to help their youngest son and would have to be sold. To keep her from having to leave Avonlea, Marilla invited her to move into Green Gables. Rachel accepted and moved into the spare room, where she took over household duties and assisted Marilla with raising the twins, Davy and Dora. She later traveled to Four Winds to visit Anne and Gilbert and share holiday dinners with them.

Over the years, she offered advice to Matthew and Marilla, helped sew dresses for Anne, and took home first prize for butter and cheese at the Exhibition. After her husband Thomas grew ill and died, Rachel learned that their farm was heavily mortgaged to help their youngest son and would have to be sold. To keep her from having to leave Avonlea, Marilla invited her to move into Green Gables. Rachel accepted and moved into the spare room, where she took over household duties and assisted Marilla with raising the twins, Davy and Dora. She later traveled to Four Winds to visit Anne and Gilbert and share holiday dinners with them.

label: History
value: Jonas Blake was a theological student
unit: Jonas Blake was a theological student from St. Columbia who took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church for a summer. During his time at St. Columbia, he befriended Philippa Gordon, spending time fishing, boating, and walking together. Although he had long tried to avoid entering the ministry, he ultimately committed himself to the work. He frequently visited Patty's Place while traveling from St. Columbia and gained the affection of the household. Over time, he fell in love with Phil and proposed to her, giving her advice on decision-making. After meeting Phil's family, he won over both of her parents, and they were married the following June. By the time of Anne Shirley's wedding, Jonas and Phil had children, and he assisted in Anne's wedding ceremony by offering a praised wedding prayer.

She passed away quietly in her sleep during the summer break.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees as the first female teacher in Avonlea. She introduced innovative teaching methods, including morning and evening physical culture exercises, nature study field days in the woods, and bi-weekly recitation afternoons. She established strong, encouraging relationships with her students, guiding them on their reading habits and moral development. Later, she organized a Queen's class to prepare interested pupils for the Entrance examination to Queen's Academy, drilling them thoroughly throughout the term. Her teaching was completely successful, as every member of her Queen's class passed the Entrance examinations. She concluded her term at Avonlea school at the end of June, leaving her pupils tearful and grateful for her guidance.

label: History
value: Susan Baker is an elderly spinster
unit: Susan Baker, an elderly spinster from the Glen, was installed as maid-of-all-work for Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley at their small house. She took complete charge of running the household, cooking, and looking after Anne's well-being. She formed a quick liking for Owen Ford after he praised her strawberry shortcake. When her sister Matilda broke her leg, Susan temporarily left her duties to go and nurse her. She also vigilantly guarded the house and baby against perceived dangers like stray cats and advised Anne on matters of marriage and practical living.
